A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RVPT study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional experiments and checklist in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original backdoor-defense experiments, perturbation-resistivity measurements, ablations, qualitative analyses and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds image-captioning and text-to-image retrieval experiments in Table 7.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP backbone, deep visual prompts, feature-repelling loss and cross-entropy objective remain unchanged. The new downstream evaluations do not document a revised RVPT procedure; Gaussian prompt initialization is newly disclosed implementation information.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds image captioning on MSCOCO and text-to-image retrieval on vision-language-enriched ImageNet-1K. These introduce substantially different task requirements beyond the retained classification, attack and generalization evaluations.

E2.justification: VPT and no-defense comparator entries for the multi-scenario FR-loss study in v2 Figure 4 disappear, including unseen-target, cross-dataset and cross-domain comparisons. New Table 7 compares RVPT with CleanCLIP and VPT. Comparator sets in the retained classification and architecture tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added captioning evaluation uses LLaVA-1.5 (13B) with ViT-L/14, target-mention ASR and BLEU. Retrieval uses ViT-B/32, one poisoned candidate, top-10 attack success, rank ratio and top-1 clean matching. Existing default training settings, including 16 shots and 50 epochs, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 removes the dedicated multi-scenario FR-loss ablation in v2 Figure 4 and the prompt-token attention maps from v2 Figure 5. Figure 3(f) merely labels the existing no-repulsion endpoint as VPT. The other sensitivity, architecture, handcrafted-prompt, perturbation-resistivity and adversarial-attack analyses remain.

E5.justification: No new seed information, repeated-run protocol, uncertainty estimates or significance tests are supplied. The added checklist claims statistical significance by citing variation of hyperparameters, but those sweeps already appeared in v2 and do not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports RVPT ASR of 0% for both captioning and retrieval, versus CleanCLIP's 23.03% and 13.33%, and VPT's 81.21% and 22.67%. These are new-task results, not improvements over v2 under matching settings. The ten existing tables retain their numerical values; the separate multi-scenario FR-loss results are removed.

T1.justification: The PR definition, threat assumptions, prompt formulation and loss equations retain their mathematical content. Exponential notation changes and moving the margin equation inline are presentational. No new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central vulnerability explanation, RVPT contribution, parameter-efficiency claim and defense/generalization claims. The additional experiments broaden supporting evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendices F–G add explicit discussion of clean-data availability, misuse and applicability limits. Section 4.5 interprets the new experiments as demonstrating defense transfer to captioning and retrieval while preserving clean performance. Existing explanations of domain-shift degradation and lack of adversarial-example robustness remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents zero-mean Gaussian prompt initialization and provides the enriched-ImageNet data reference. It removes the explicit RVPT code link, the 1,000-image PR sample count and Appendix D.3's ablation settings. The checklist asserts open access without restoring the code link; most existing implementation and compute details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to test-time multimodal defenses, including BDetCLIP, and recent attacks such as VL-Trojan and BadToken, plus sources for the added datasets. Related work briefly acknowledges test-time defenses, while the central positioning of RVPT as a post-training prompt-based defense remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The PR motivation is locally rewritten, captions are shortened, and attention-map/t-SNE discussion is condensed under the renamed 'Further Explorations' section. The appendix outline expands and impact, limitations and checklist sections are appended. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper switches from two columns to one. PR panels are reordered, Table 6 is restructured, the separate FR-loss figure is removed, and attention/t-SNE displays are reworked and placed side by side. Table 7 is added; its caption and header give conflicting rank-ratio direction arrows.

improvement.justification: Table 7 adds directly relevant evidence of defense transfer to captioning and retrieval, while Appendix G clarifies applicability limits. This modestly strengthens the paper. Gains are constrained by sparse new-experiment details and removal of multi-scenario FR controls and the code link. Clean-performance preservation also needs qualification: caption BLEU is 4.51 versus 6.22 without defense.
